title: [DECISION] Dual-source rejection prevents ambiguous IKM selection
description: src/cdev/crypto2dev_fd.c lines 1842-1854: DO_KDF rejects any call where both ikm_fd \!= -1 AND state->inbuf_len > 0. This is a clear error: the caller has written IKM data (method A) but also provided ikm_fd (method B). Rather than silently choosing one, the implementation returns -EINVAL. This non-obvious check prevents silent failures where a mistaken dual-source call succeeds with undefined behavior (which source is used?). The framework comment explicitly states the rationale: 'ikm_fd path: require no pending write() data (dual-source rejected). write() path: require at least one byte of accumulated write() data.' This is purely defensive — it cannot happen with correct usage, but when it does, the failure is loud and unambiguous.
